texts: doha: guy rides in a palanquin dressed as a saint just so people take pictures of him
A doha on the man carried in a decorated palanquin through the streets, in the clothes of holiness, folding his hands for the crowd and holding the pose as long as the cameras are pointed at him.
In a palanquin of petals he is carried, a saint for the afternoon.
At my brother-in-law's society event he was carried in a palanquin like a holy man, and as soon as the cameras went off he lit a cigarette. Could you write a doha?
palanquin, holiness for show
A doha on the crow in white feathers painted for the festival, sitting very still at the edge of the crowd, looking holy and calm, while his eye searches the ground for crumbs.
doha: crow acting like a saint when people are looking
The crow folds its wings as if in prayer, but its eye is on the crumbs of the crowd.
crow, fake calm
A man at the park sits very still with eyes closed whenever people pass, and I saw him open one eye like a crow to check if anyone is watching. A doha for him?
doha: the cleric ties a rope to his waist and stands in public as a show of discipline
A doha on the cleric who ties a rope around himself and stands for hours in public view as a sign of devotion, and who is quick to leave the moment the crowd thins and no one is watching.
Around the cleric's waist a rope of discipline, around his eyes a veil of vanity.
The cleric at our fair stood in the open heat with a rope around his waist for the whole afternoon, took breaks behind the tent when no one looked, and took donations by evening. A doha?
cleric, rope, performance
Every Diwali my neighbour lights dozens of lamps outside his gate, invites everyone to see them, and puts out all but one the second the guests leave. Doha?
A doha about the one who lights a hundred lamps at the front for the neighbours to see, for his reputation of piety, while his heart remains dark, and the inner lamp that matters is not lit.
doha: lots of lamps for show, nothing lit inside
A hundred lamps burn at his gate, but inside him all is dark.
lamp, display, dark heart
He sits like a statue in prayer while the priest announces his piety, and the seed of true devotion has not even been sown.
A doha about the rich man who pays the priest to announce his donation and prayer loudly to the whole gathering, scattering seeds of grain for the cameras while his heart remains a barren field.
seed, priest, public piety
At our community meeting the priest called out the name of every donor and the rich man scattered seeds for the birds in front of the cameras, and went home and shooed away a hungry old man. A doha?
doha: priest announces the donation, rich guy throws seeds for photos, no real heart
The furnace roars in the potter's yard unseen; the beggar's show roars in the street to be seen.
A doha on the fake beggar who sits near the furnace outside the pilgrim's road and puts on a face of holiness, smeared with dust, to earn the coins of those who think he is a holy man.
furnace, beggar, performance
A beggar near the furnace on our road sits with his eyes closed in a holy pose when pilgrims pass, but chats with the shopkeepers when no one is there. A doha?
doha: fake beggar acting holy near the furnace for coins
cuckoo, dew, show
Our colony singer sings like a cuckoo at the event and weeps real dew when people applaud, but he is spiteful in the lane. A doha?
Dew on the cheek when the crowd is near, a cuckoo's song for the listener, and silence in the heart.
A doha on the performer with the voice of a cuckoo who sings devotional songs for the audience, with tears like morning dew when the applause begins, though nothing moves within.
doha: cuckoo voice and fake dew tears for the audience
ash, cuckoo, pretend
A doha on the one who smears ash on his body and sings sweetly like a cuckoo before a gathering, putting on a show of renunciation, while the real flame of devotion has never been lit in him.
Ash on his body and a cuckoo's tune on his lips, the stage is set but the heart is not.
The famous singer in our city smears ash on his forehead and sings like a cuckoo at every event, then charges a fortune and complains about the food. A doha?
doha: ash on the body and a cuckoo voice, all for the show
doha: fire ritual with the crow watching, people performing for the camera
fire, crow, performance
The fire is lit for the cameras, the crow watches from the wall, and the Lord is not invited.
At the public fire ceremony, the host kept looking at the cameras instead of the fire, and a crow stole the offering. A doha?
A doha on the fire ritual held in front of a crowd with elaborate gestures for the cameras, while a crow on the wall watches the false performance and takes the offering for itself.
A doha on the man carried in a palanquin up the mountain path in the robes of a pilgrim, who looks holy to the crowd but has never walked a single step of the penance himself.
doha: rich guy pilgrimage in a palanquin up a mountain, not a real pilgrim
palanquin, mountain, pilgrim
The politician went up the mountain in a palanquin carried by four men to be photographed as a pilgrim, and complained about the cold. Could you write a doha?
Carried on a palanquin up the mountain, he calls it a pilgrimage and the bearers call it work.
holiness for an audience
doha: people who pray only when someone is watching
My colleague closes his eyes and chants whenever the boss walks by, and the rest of the time talks about stock prices. Doha for him?
A doha on the person who prays only when watched, folding his hands the moment a visitor arrives, and forgetting the Lord the moment the visitor leaves, because his audience was never the Lord.
His prayers begin with the audience and end with the applause.
Seeds of charity thrown where the cameras can see them, and the harvest he wants is applause.
A doha on the donor who scatters a seed here and there before the crowd with a grand announcement, wanting his name sung, and who never plants anything that will grow when he is not looked at.
doha: donating a seed of kindness with cameras around, wanting praise
A man donated blankets at our colony event with a banner of his own face, and a seed of kindness is not hidden anymore. A doha?
seed, charity for show

A doha about the person who posts photographs of every act of worship and charity on the internet, counting likes as blessings, while the real act remains forgotten and the Lord is not the one liking the post.
posting piety online
doha: posting your prayers on social media for likes
My cousin posts a photo of himself praying every morning with a caption about gratitude, but he has not spoken to his mother in a year. A doha?
Prayer posted for the likes, a heart left on mute.
A doha on the proud man with the roar of a lion who recites holy words so everyone can hear his tongue's devotion, but whose devotion stops when the audience goes home.
doha: lion roars about his piety and the tongue says holy things for the crowd
lion, tongue, show
The lion of piety roars from the tongue and not from the heart.
The loud man at our gathering who holds forth like a lion about devotion speaks sweetly from his tongue to everyone's face, and cheats them in business. Could you write a doha?
The swan is white by nature; the washerman whitens the cloth for the crowd.
A doha about the washerman who dresses in a swan's white and stands in public with a holy face, looking pure to the crowd, though the dirt of his own mind has never been washed.
doha: washerman in swan white acting holy in public
swan, washerman, show
The washerman's son wears all white and acts serious at the public events, as if he were a swan among sparrows, but he's the first to gossip. A doha?
stone, forehead mark, display
doha: holy forehead mark, stone idol, performance for the crowd
My boss makes a show of kneeling in front of a stone image and applying a forehead mark whenever clients are around. A doha?
A forehead mark for the crowd, a stone to bow to, and no one to bow to in the heart.
A doha on the one who puts on the bright forehead mark and kneels before a stone idol in public with a loud flourish, so that all may see how pious he is, but never kneels in private.
He wears his holiness like a good coat, for show and when the weather asks.
holy for the crowd
A doha on the person who puts on holiness in front of the watchers as one puts on a coat, and takes it off the moment the guests go, wearing a different face in private.
A man in our locality acts devout only in front of the elders and the rest of the time is a gambler. Could you write a doha?
doha: acting holy just for the people who watch
The moth burns without an audience, and the pious burns with one.
An actor in our drama group played a devout moth in a play, and the audience wept, but offstage he is always pretending. Doha idea?
moth, devotion on stage
A doha on the moth that gives its life for the light without a single watcher, and the man who does everything for show, giving nothing to the Lord unless a crowd is present.
doha: the moth circles the flame for love, not for the crowd, unlike people
doha about people doing charity only when they get their name on a plaque
A name on a plaque; a gift weighed in applause.
donor's plaque
A doha about the man who gives to the poor only if his name is carved on the wall for all to read, as if the Lord could only read marble and not the hidden hand.
The family that donated a bench to the park insisted on a big plaque with their name on it, and yet they haven't spoken to the family next to them in ten years. A doha?
He fed the crowd milk and wanted their praise; the poor child at his gate got no milk at all.
milk, charity, show
doha: giving out milk for the cameras, nothing for the poor kid at home
The mayor had milk distributed at the fair with his posters on every can, but the milkman who works every day is still unpaid. Doha?
A doha on the donor who distributes milk to the crowd in front of the cameras with his name on every cup, and walks past the hungry child at his own gate without a thought.
A doha on the parrot in a palace, taught to say holy words in front of guests, which the king shows off as a mark of his devotion, though neither the parrot nor the king knows what the words mean.
The rich family's parrot, kept in a palace-like mansion, recites prayers on cue when guests arrive, and the family brags about it. A doha for them?
In the palace the parrot recites the holy names for guests, and the master takes the praise.
parrot, palace, show
doha: the parrot in the palace says holy words for guests
The thief in my neighbourhood put up a big religious banner on his house and invites everyone to ceremonies, while he plans the next robbery. A doha?
The house of the thief is hung with holy flags, and the neighbours are invited to bow.
A doha on the thief who decorates his house with holy symbols and invites the whole street to his prayers, so that no one will suspect him of anything while his mind plans the next theft.
doha: thief with a holy house, looks pious, is not
thief, house, holy banner
piety for an audience
At the meeting, a man stood up and began to cry about his devotion, turned to see whether everyone was watching, and then cried harder. Doha for that?
He wept in public and watched who was watching.
write a doha: crying in front of people to look devout
A doha on the one who weeps and trembles in the presence of onlookers when he speaks of the Lord, whose tears dry up the moment he is alone, and who checks the crowd to see if it is moved.
At the cremation ground, the man who owns three factories rang a bell for everyone to hear as a gesture of respect, and then complained that the pyre was too small. A doha?
bell, cremation ground, show
He rings the bell at the cremation ground, so all can hear; what he hears himself is only the sound.
doha: ringing the bell at the cremation ground just so people notice him
A doha on the mourner who rings a bell very loudly at the cremation ground, performing his grief and devotion for the crowd, though his thoughts are on the will and the property of the dead.
My aunt does her puja on the balcony facing the street so the neighbours can see how devoted she is, while she skips it on rainy days. A doha?
She prays on the balcony facing the road, and on rainy days the Lord waits indoors.
balcony prayer
A doha on the person who performs his devotion at a spot where the maximum number of people will see him, and relocates the whole rite out of sight whenever the crowd is gone.
doha: praying where everyone can see
A doha on the man who sits in a famous pose of meditation on the road with a signboard announcing his silence, and whose eyes open the moment anyone offers a coin or a camera.
doha: meditating with a signboard
Eyes closed for the crowd, open for the coin.
meditation for coins
A man near the station sits in meditation with a sign saying 'silent for world peace' and opens his eyes every time someone drops a coin. Doha?
A doha on the beggar who dresses as a holy man and sits at the roadside with a sacred expression, because he has learned that people give more to piety than to need, and his holiness is a trade.
The beggar learns to look holy, for holiness sells better than hunger.
A beggar at the corner learned to chant loudly when nicely dressed people walk by and goes quiet when the street is empty. A doha for him?
beggar, holy act
doha: beggar who puts on a holy face for more money
A thread round the neck of the holy, a tree planted for the press, and no shade for anyone.
thread, tree, photo opportunity
A doha on the leader who ties a holy thread and plants a tree in front of the press cameras, and never waters it, and whose piety lasts exactly as long as the photograph.
The politician planted a tree and tied a thread round it for the cameras and never came back. The tree is dead now. Can you write a doha?
doha: tree planting with a thread tied for the camera, never watered
A doha on the one who dresses in the finest cotton of simple living and speaks of detachment before an admiring audience, while his closets are full and his heart is full of desire.
The simplest cotton for the public eye; for the private life, silk.
My neighbour wears rough cotton clothes in public and brags about his simple life, and I saw his closet full of expensive imports. Doha?
cotton, simple living show
doha: wearing simple cotton for show
A bridge of promises built for the cameras, and a net of words to catch the votes.
doha: bridge opening ceremony and net of promises, fake piety
A doha on the leader who opens a bridge with a grand prayer ceremony and holy words, casting a net of promises over the crowd, though the bridge is shoddy and his piety is only for the occasion.
bridge, net, ceremony
The official blessed the new bridge with a loud prayer ceremony, and spread a net of promises to the crowd, and the bridge collapsed in six months. A doha?
The potter in our colony is praised for his devotion at every festival, because he makes beautiful clay idols and plays a one-string lute for the crowd, but he is cruel to his apprentices. A doha?
A doha on the potter who shapes clay with great flourish before an audience and plays a one-string lute to show his devotion, though his true work is done in silence, and the show is for applause.
doha: potter and clay and a one-string lute, all for the audience
potter and clay, lute, show
He shapes the clay for the crowd, plays the one-string lute for the crowd, and for himself plays nothing.
A doha on the donor who hands out jaggery sweets in public with a loud announcement of his generosity, wanting every cheek to praise him, though the real sweetness of giving lies in doing it quietly.
jaggery, charity for show
doha: giving out jaggery and posting it everywhere
My uncle distributed jaggery sweets at the bus stop and made sure a photographer was there. He hasn't given a rupee to his own brother. Doha?
He gave jaggery to the crowd, but the sweetness was meant for himself.
In our colony the man who runs the prayer group likes to hold it right outside, so everybody sees him, and tells the neighbours about how many people attend. A doha?
He holds the prayers where the eyes are, so that the Lord may be an afterthought.
prayer group for status
doha: holding prayers in public for status
A doha on the one who organises public prayers and festivals mainly to be seen at the front, seating himself in the centre, taking the garland, and leaving before the real work begins.
holy gestures, empty heart
doha about showing off how holy you are
Folded hands, bowed head, and a heart standing straight and proud.
My friend folds his hands and bows his head dramatically when entering any room with religious people, but is rude to waiters. A doha for him?
A doha on the person who knows every gesture of piety, the folded hands, the bowed head, the lowered eyes, and performs them nicely, but who has never once lowered his pride.
He bows with his body for the world, and keeps his heart upright for himself.
doha: bowing for the crowd
bowing for show
Our local leader bows deeply to every elder at the function and then calls them fools in the car. Doha?
A doha on the man who bows deeply to every important person at a gathering and holds his head high among the humble, as though respect were something to be spent where it brings a return.
potter and clay, public show
doha: potter spinning clay for tourists, claiming it's his holy work
The potter at the heritage village makes a big show of worship before working, for the tourists, and uses a machine at night. A doha?
A doha on the potter who shapes clay in front of tourists with a flourish, saying it is a holy craft handed down for ages, while the work he sells is machine made and the holiness is a story.
The potter shapes the clay in front of tourists, with a speech about holiness he does not believe.
doha: the saint who loves cameras more than God
He dims the lights of his own devotion to shine in the cameras' glare.
saint for cameras
A doha on the holy man who arranges the camera angles before beginning his sermon, adjusts his robe for the photographs, and speaks of humility in a voice meant to carry across the crowd.
The visiting preacher checked the lighting and camera angles before his talk on humility, and posed for ten minutes afterwards. What would Kabir say?
doha about those who pray to be seen praying
They kneel where the light is best, and bend as the crowd turns.
My neighbour always chooses the front row at religious events and turns around to see who has come in. A doha for him?
A doha on the ones who choose their place of prayer by where the crowd is thickest, kneeling in the best light and glancing around to see who is watching, as though the audience were the Lord.
praying to be seen

A doha on the musk deer which carries the scent within it, quietly, never boasting, and the man who stands before a stone image in the public eye to announce his devotion to the world, with no fragrance within.
doha: musk deer carries scent quietly, human holiness is stone cold for the audience
The musk deer wears its fragrance within; the man wears his holiness on the stone for all to see.
A man in our area bows before a stone idol loudly when the neighbours pass, and a musk deer in the nearby sanctuary wanders silently, carrying its fragrance within. A doha for the contrast?
musk deer, stone, show
doha: palanquin and a lamp lit for a photo, no real devotion
lamp, palanquin, show
The lamp is lit for the photograph, the palanquin is carried for the crowd, and the Lord sits unseen.
At my cousin's reception he arrived in a palanquin and lit a lamp for a ceremony for exactly the time it took to take photos. A doha?
A doha on the groom or the leader who is carried in a palanquin and lights a ceremonial lamp in front of the cameras, and who has no thought for the Lord or the guests beyond the photograph.
devotion as theatre
A doha on the person who stages his devotion as a theatre performance, with costumes, music, and applause, forgetting that the Lord is not an audience member and was never fooled by costumes.
Our annual religious event has turned into a competition of costumes and drama, and the real prayer is lost. A doha?
doha: religion has become a drama
The stage is set and the costumes are ready; only the Lord has not been told.
The man who sits in the front row at every sermon never listens, he is busy scanning the crowd to see who is noticing him. A doha?
A doha on the man who appears in the front row at every sermon and nods vigorously at the speaker, to be noticed, and sleeps through the wisdom in the speaker's words.
doha about nodding in front-row seats to be noticed
front row piety
He nods at the words he does not hear, for the eyes he hopes will see.
The date palm bears its fruit high and quiet, while the man at its foot proclaims his devotion to the passing crowd.
A doha on the date palm that stands tall and gives sweet fruit without announcing it, and the man who stands under it proclaiming his holiness to all passers by, but who bears no fruit.
doha: date palm gives fruit quietly, people give loudly
date palm, quiet giving
Under the date palm in our village sits a man who tells everyone he gives to charity, though no one has ever seen what he gives. Doha?
doha: the yogi poses for tourists
A doha on the yogi who has learned to strike a pose of deep meditation whenever tourists arrive, and to relax the moment the buses leave, because his stillness is a performance for coin.
Still as a yogi's statue for the buses, and a talker when they leave.
The yogi at the ghat meditates dramatically as the tourist launches come in and chats happily when they leave. What would Kabir say?
yogi, posing
crow, net, pretending
The crow sits in holy silence over the net, but his eye measures the feast.
doha: crow acting like a saint beside a net of grain
A doha on the crow who sits in a saintly posture near the net, as though he has renounced all grain, but whose only thought is how to take the bait without being caught.
A man at the grain stalls sits meditating beside the net, and a crow sat next to him, and I could not tell which one was after the grain. A doha?
A doha on the skeleton of a rotting reputation, hidden behind a lavish ceremony held on the bridge to the holy place, where the host pretends to piety while the whole town knows his secrets.
A skeleton in the cupboard, a prayer on the bridge, a mask on the face.
doha: skeleton and a bridge and pretending to be holy
The man who led the ceremony at the bridge opening has a skeleton in his closet that everyone knows about, and still he speaks of purity. A doha?
skeleton, bridge, pretence
The speaker at the event used the sweetest, most holy phrases, and then insulted the cook in the kitchen. His tongue knew which audience was in front of it. A doha?
tongue, holy words, audience
A doha on the tongue that speaks sweet and holy words only when someone important is listening, and turns sour and sharp in the kitchen, so that the speech belongs to the audience and not the heart.
doha: sweet-talking holy words to the audience, nasty tongue backstage
The tongue is sweet in the hall and sharp in the kitchen.
judging others publicly
A doha on the person who stands in judgement over every other pilgrim, correcting their rituals and pointing out their flaws in a loud voice, to display his own knowledge of holiness to the audience.
He points to the dust on others' feet to hide the dust on his own.
At the gathering, one man spent the entire time correcting everyone else's way of worshipping, loudly, to impress the elders. A doha?
doha: judging others publicly to look holy
A doha on the person who gives to the poor in the morning on the steps of the holy place before everyone, and cheats the same poor in his store in the afternoon, his piety as short as the morning.
The grocer gives out free food at the holy place every morning for the crowd to see, and in the afternoon he sells spoiled grain. A doha?
morning charity, afternoon cheat
doha: fake charity in the morning, cheating in the afternoon
Charity in the morning for the crowd, short weight in the afternoon for the poor.
doha: ocean of show, jaggery of piety, sweetness only on the surface
ocean, jaggery, display
A doha on the one whose piety is an ocean of display, with waves of ceremony and speeches, but is thin as a coat of jaggery on a bitter pill, sweet only to the eye.
At the grand event by the ocean, the host gave out jaggery sweets to everyone and a long speech on devotion, but his staff say he has not paid wages for months. A doha?
An ocean of display and a lump of jaggery of piety; sweet on the surface, bitter beneath.
